raw_cue_correspondence.text: Open the department menu and choose Stations and Groups.
The table separates each group’s type, parent, and member count.
Our fictional Chicago Fire department already has a station and
organizational groups beneath it.
We will add an empty coordination parent and a separate
station beneath that parent.
Read the existing rows first so the new exercise is easy to identify and
the original memberships remain intact.
Choose Add New Group and keep Organizational Group selected.
Enter Training Only, Community Coordination, followed
by the exercise date.
Parent Group remains None, making this a top-level group.
Group Admins and Group Users stay empty.
These fields describe different membership responsibilities; choosing an
administrator is a permission decision.
We are preparing a structure, so we do not move a person from an existing
group or assign an administrator.
Use Save Group.
The fresh Edit Group readback retains its full name and Parent None, and displays
the Organizational type read-only.
Both membership selectors remain empty.
The page explains that a person can belong to only one group at a time.
required_labels: Users can only be in one group at a time. If you don't see your user in the list they are already in a group.

spoken_references.Users can only be in one group at a time: only one group at a time

raw_cue_correspondence.text: When maintaining a populated group, let its existing selections load before
saving: the form submits the complete member and administrator selection.
Create another group and select Station Group.
Name it Training Only, Community Base, with the exercise date, and choose the
new coordination group as its parent.
A station requires a physical reference location.
The form offers address fields, a coordinate pair, or a what3words address.
We will use an explicitly illustrative Chicago coordinate pair.
The parent describes the organizational relationship; it does not replace
the station’s own location.
In Gps Coordinates, enter latitude forty-one point eight five and longitude
minus eighty-seven point six five.
Enter both values together.
The street fields are unused and what3words stays blank.
This is a typed station reference, not a device-location reading or
proof that anyone arrived there.
Keep the member and administrator selectors empty and leave
printing unconfigured.
Use Save Group once after checking the prepared values.
The returned catalog shows both new groups with zero members.
The organizational root has no parent, while the station
names that root as its parent.
Use the station’s Edit control to check its full name and relationship again.
Scroll to verify the saved coordinate pair, blank what3words field, and
clear Print Calls to Printer option.
This readback checks the particular fields we stored without changing the
station type or configuring printing.
Open Units and choose New Unit.
The form separates Name, Type, Station, and the unit’s role positions.
No Station is available, but our exercise will use the station we just created.
A role position defines a seat; it does not select the person occupying that seat.
Before completing this unit, use the type link to create a distinct
training vehicle type that will be recognizable in the unit list.
From the Unit Types section, choose New Unit Type.
Enter Training Only, Community Response Vehicle.
Set Class to Support; the help explains that class is used for
reports, defaults, and integrations, separately from the display name.
Keep Actions on Standard Actions and choose Van for Map Icon.
The optional custom-icon file remains empty.
These choices define the new type without changing an existing
type or a department status set.
The preview now shows the built-in green Van symbol on light and
dark backgrounds and in a list.
No custom image has been uploaded.
Save, then read the new type row in the catalog.
It shows the full name, Default Unit Actions, and Van.
Open Edit to verify Support, Standard Actions, and the Van choice again.
This confirms the type configuration; it is not a demonstration of
a vehicle’s live map location.
Return to New Unit and name the vehicle Training Only, Community
Van, with the exercise date.
Select the new type and station.
Add two positions with different names.
Coordination Seat requires the existing Community Response Navigator personnel
role, and its Required box is checked.
Optional Support Seat has no personnel-role restriction
and its Required box is clear.
These are the unit’s seat definitions.
No person is assigned by creating either row.
Browse Templates opens reusable starting layouts.
Here the Security Companies cards show examples such as Security
Patrol and Alarm Response Team.
Use These Roles would add a template’s positions to the
form for review before saving.
For this exercise, choose Close instead.
The settled unit form still contains our two prepared positions.
Inspect a template’s suggested roles deliberately rather than
assuming its names or suggested qualifications match your department.
Use Save on the prepared unit.
The returned list shows its full name and training vehicle type.
Open Edit and check that both positions and their Required choices remain.
Open the Station dropdown to read the complete selected Community Base
name; the closed field truncates it.
We are verifying the stored definition without pressing Update.
The list’s Available display alone does not establish crew readiness or
prove a newly recorded status event.
Open Unit Staffing to distinguish positions from assigned people.
Engine fifty-one retains Herrmann in its one configured seat.
The new van is Not Staffed, and both positions are Not Occupied.
Opening a person selector does not itself prove that the listed
people hold the required role.
We close it without selecting anyone.
Save on this page replaces staffing selections across the department,
so we leave it untouched and preserve every existing assignment.
Finish with the group tree on Units.
Expand and select the Community Coordination parent.
Its view includes the vehicle assigned to the child Community Base station.
Select that station directly and the same unit appears.
This demonstrates the saved relationship from organizational
parent to station to unit.
These tree choices filter the view; they do not move a unit, assign a
crew member, or change its status.
Chicago Fire can separate a coordination structure from a station and its vehicles.
Community care and mental health teams can organize operational teams
and bases without patient detail.
Search and rescue can distinguish coordination groups, staging bases,
and resources; security teams can structure patrol resources; wildland
teams can organize seasonal bases; and industrial response teams can separate
facility groups from response vehicles.
In each setting, verify saved relationships and seat requirements,
then manage actual staffing as a separate, deliberate operation.
